details:
SOLAR AFRICA – Satellite Intelligence for a Safer and Sustainable Africa

Solar Africa is an AI-powered environmental and agricultural intelligence platform designed to address critical climate, energy, and food-security challenges affecting Rwanda and other African countries. It combines NASA Earth observation data, artificial intelligence, interactive maps, farm-level analytics, and community reports to support data-driven decision-making and sustainable development.

How the Project Works

Solar Africa is built around five integrated modules and a dedicated farmer decision-support experience:

  1. Solar Africa (Clean Energy Intelligence): Uses NASA POWER data to analyze solar radiation, temperature, and rainfall, helping communities and renewable energy developers identify high-potential locations for solar energy deployment.
  2. WasteWatch Africa (Environmental & Plastic Monitoring): Supports plastic waste tracking by collecting community reports, geolocated photographs, and field observations to identify illegal dumping sites and prioritize areas requiring environmental investigation.
  3. Drone4Africa (Aerial Mapping & Logistics): Supports precision agricultural monitoring, medical delivery route planning, environmental conservation, and waste inspections through automated drone mission planning and aerial image analysis.
    • Yield & Production Tracking: View total harvest amounts alongside daily, monthly, and seasonal production trends across different crops.
    • Plot-Level Mapping & Soil Intelligence: Select specific land plots on an interactive map to track soil health metrics (such as moisture, pH, and nutrient balance) tailored to each crop.
    • AI Plant Diagnostics & Actionable Recommendations: Upload plant photos for instant AI-assisted crop health checks and receive timely, practical guidance on irrigation, fertilization, pest control, and soil remediation.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project promotes clean energy adoption, strengthens environmental protection, boosts smallholder agricultural productivity, enhances disaster preparedness, and improves community safety. By translating complex satellite data and local field observations into clear, everyday guidance, Solar Africa empowers farmers, local authorities, organizations, and citizens to make timely, informed decisions.

Our long-term vision is to launch and validate the platform in Rwanda before scaling across Africa to build resilient communities and sustainable food and energy systems.

Tools and Technologies

  • Earth Observation & Satellite Data: NASA POWER, NASA Landsat, NASA EMIT, NASA GPM, NASA LHASA, and NASA FIRMS.
  • Software & AI Stack: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, interactive geospatial mapping tools, and Google’s Gemini AI (for multimodal plant diagnostics and agronomic recommendations).
  • Field & Access Hardware: Designed for responsive web and mobile access, supported by smartphones and drones for field data capture and environmental monitoring.

Creativity and Innovation

Solar Africa unifies renewable energy, waste management, drone operations, disaster awareness, and precision farming within a single ecosystem. Rather than presenting raw satellite data, its innovative approach transforms space-based observations, plot-level soil metrics, and community or farmer inputs into practical, step-by-step recommendations that everyday users can act on immediately.

Factors Considered

The platform is designed around affordability, mobile accessibility, data accuracy, environmental sustainability, community participation, user privacy, and public safety. Recognizing the limitations of satellite resolution and automated diagnostics, Solar Africa treats AI-generated insights and satellite-based risk alerts as decision-support tools—encouraging confirmation by local agronomists and relevant authorities before critical interventions.

Solar Africa’s ultimate goal is to bridge space technology, artificial intelligence, and grassroots action to build a cleaner, more food-secure, and sustainable Africa.
